h1: Maternity hospital software for a stay that was booked nine months in advance.
sub: A maternity hospital plans almost everything. Antenatal visits build one record over months, the admission date is known, the stay is billed as a package, and the baby arrives as a second record linked to the mother. HIMS is set up for that shape of work.

sections.h2: What makes maternity different from general inpatient care
paras: Maternity is the most predictable inpatient work a hospital does. The patient is known months before she is admitted, she is seen repeatedly during that time, the admission has an expected date, the stay has an expected length, and the charge is usually agreed as a package rather than counted item by item at the end. Hospital software for maternity is therefore less about emergency capacity and more about holding one long record and billing a stay that was priced before it started.

HIMS handles this with the same parts it uses everywhere: one UHID that carries every antenatal visit, appointments that book the next review before the patient leaves, bed and theatre scheduling for the admission, package billing for the stay, and a second patient record for the newborn linked to the mother's. The newborn is described here as a linked record, because that is what it is. There is no separate neonatal module on record, and anything beyond a linked record is scoped on the call.

sections.h2: Everything about the case was known in advance, and the bill is still assembled at the door.
sections.lead: Maternity work spans months, and paper does not span months well.

items.h: The antenatal card lives with the patient
items.p: If she forgets it, the hospital has no history, and the visit starts from nothing.

items.h: The package is agreed and then argued about
items.p: What is inside the package and what is extra was explained once, verbally, and nobody wrote it against the case.
A scan or a review due in three weeks depends on the patient remembering, and there is no list of who did not come.
Observations and feeds are written on the mother's sheet, so the newborn has nothing to be discharged with.
Discharge is the moment the TPA paperwork starts, and the family is already packed.

sections.h2: How a maternity case runs on one record.

steps.p: The mother is registered under a UHID; the visit, investigations and notes attach to it.
Each review adds to the same record, with the next appointment booked before she leaves and a WhatsApp reminder set.
The expected date is on the appointment list, the bed is allocated and the package and payer are recorded at admission.
A planned procedure is scheduled on the theatre list; an unplanned one is added on the day.
The baby is registered as a patient in their own right and linked to the mother's record.
Nursing notes, drugs issued from the pharmacy and anything outside the package accrue on the bill.
Two summaries, one bill settled against the package, insurance or TPA documents pulled from the record.

items.q: Does HIMS have an obstetrics module?
items.a: HIMS is a general hospital system configured for the way a maternity hospital works, which is long planned stays, months of antenatal visits on one record and package billing. It is not sold as a specialty product, and anything specialty-specific is scoped on the call rather than claimed here.

The newborn is registered as a patient with their own record, linked to the mother's admission, so notes and a discharge summary belong to the baby. This is a linked record rather than a neonatal module, and further requirements are discussed during scoping.

items.q: Can a delivery package be billed as one item?
items.a: Yes. The package sits on the admission and anything provided outside it is billed separately and visibly. See hospital package billing software for how packages and extras are handled.

items.q: Will antenatal visits stay on the same record for months?
items.a: Yes. Every visit attaches to one UHID, so a consultant opening the record sees the whole sequence of visits, investigations and prescriptions rather than the most recent one.

items.q: Does it handle insurance and TPA for a delivery?
items.a: Yes. Pre-authorisation is recorded at admission and claim documents come from the record at discharge. See TPA billing software.

items.q: Can patients book and see reports themselves?
items.a: Yes. The patient app and portal show upcoming appointments and reports, and reminders for reviews can go out on WhatsApp with templates agreed at setup.

items.p: A stay priced as one item.
